articles.headline: The many faces of Summerhall fear being priced out by hotel plans
articles.summary: Artists and makers based at Summerhall, the Edinburgh arts venue, say they fear being unable to afford to stay once the planned hotel development on the site is complete.

articles.headline: India's female bodybuilders
articles.summary: Photo-led FT Weekend feature on women in Kerala, many from conservative backgrounds, who are taking up bodybuilding, finding community and challenging gender norms.

articles.headline: Picasso called him 'the father of us all': what explains Cézanne's enduring influence?
articles.summary: Review of the Grand Palais Cézanne blockbuster in Paris, judged a strong history lesson and a stylish contemporary show, though not without flaws.

articles.headline: The secretive world of collecting passports
articles.summary: FT Collecting column on the niche market for vintage passports and travel documents: who collects them and why.

articles.headline: Caravaggio, lo straordinario teatro del vero. Il «Bacchino» che svela un lato nascosto di Dioniso
articles.headline_en: Caravaggio, the extraordinary theatre of the real: the Bacchino that reveals a hidden side of Dionysus
articles.summary: Instalment of Corriere's masterpiece series on Caravaggio's theatrical realism, reading the young Bacchus as a revealing take on Dionysus and drawing on works such as the Capodimonte Flagellation.

articles.headline: Aline et Sophie Crumb croisent leurs planches à Paris
articles.headline_en: Aline and Sophie Crumb cross their drawings in Paris
articles.summary: Review of 'En toute liberté' at the Huberty & Breyne gallery in Paris, which brings together drawings and comics pages by a mother and daughter and tells their family and artistic story with candour.

articles.headline: Switzerland's cult architect creates a new temple for art
articles.summary: Peter Zumthor's Wyss Museum, a new building for the Fondation Beyeler in Basel, pairs striking interiors with rough utilitarian concrete.

articles.headline: In the Fog of War, Native American Veteran Artists Find Inspiration
articles.summary: A show at the Wheelwright Museum of the American Indian in Santa Fe presents work by Indigenous veterans, many of whom served in Vietnam, and looks at how military service shaped their art.

articles.headline: De la tecnología futurista a la espiritualidad: Mariko Mori repasa su carrera en Tokio
articles.headline_en: From futuristic technology to spirituality: Mariko Mori surveys her career in Tokyo
articles.summary: Agency-sourced report on the Mori Art Museum's survey of Japanese artist Mariko Mori, from interactive installations to photography that fuses technology and spirituality.

articles.headline: Scudi antisommossa, manganelli e banconote con Trump, ad Artissima la creatività sfida il potere
articles.headline_en: Riot shields, batons and banknotes with Trump: at Artissima creativity challenges power
articles.summary: Video report from the Artissima contemporary art fair in Turin (30 October to 1 November), picking out politically charged works such as paint-splattered riot shields and oil-stained banknotes bearing Donald Trump's face.

articles.headline: Australia's best photos of the month: October 2026
articles.summary: Monthly gallery of standout Australian press and documentary photography from October, from a Dolly Parton theme to tulips and outback life.

articles.headline: Le Musée des Confluences expose des photographies d'œuvres aux pompes funèbres pour « accompagner les familles dans leur deuil »
articles.headline_en: The Musée des Confluences shows photographs of its works in funeral homes to 'support families in their grief'
articles.summary: Around All Saints' Day, three funeral homes in Lyon display giant photographs of Egyptian, Latin American and Caucasian artefacts from the Musée des Confluences, an outreach move meant to comfort grieving families.

articles.headline: Schön und geheimnisvoll wie Mona Lisa: So malte Franz Gertsch die Zürcher Prostituierte Lady Shiva
articles.headline_en: Beautiful and mysterious like the Mona Lisa: how Franz Gertsch painted the Zurich prostitute Lady Shiva
articles.summary: On Franz Gertsch's photorealist portrait of Irene Staub, alias Lady Shiva, a Zurich figure with ties to artists such as Sigmar Polke and H.R. Giger; the piece reads Gertsch's beauty as bound up with melancholy and transience.
articles.author: Philipp Meier

articles.headline: Up close and personal with the first known portrait of an artist's wife
articles.summary: Preview of the National Gallery's Van Eyck portraits exhibition, which will bring the painter's ten surviving portraits together for the first time, including the likeness of his wife Margaret.

articles.headline: Royal tour artist praises King Charles's energy during 'fascinating circus'
articles.summary: Jonathan Yeo, who painted the King's first official portrait, is travelling on the Caribbean royal tour as its artist, with a free brief to paint whatever inspires him.

articles.headline: Paul Stankard, an internationally acclaimed master glass artist, has died at 83
articles.summary: Paul Stankard of Mantua, New Jersey, known worldwide for botanical paperweights and small glass sculptures held by museums, died of cancer on 6 October. He also helped found the glass art programme at Salem Community College.
articles.author: Gary Miles

articles.headline: The week around the world in 20 pictures
articles.summary: Weekly selection of the week's strongest news photography, including Serbia's election, a Spanish train crash and Obama on the midterm trail.

articles.headline: Jerry Gorovoy, l'ombre fidèle de l'artiste Louise Bourgeois
articles.headline_en: Jerry Gorovoy, the faithful shadow of the artist Louise Bourgeois
articles.summary: Profile of the American who was Louise Bourgeois's assistant for almost thirty years, both protector and tireless promoter, and who still champions her work sixteen years after her death.

articles.headline: Edinburgh council to push to delay artists' eviction from St Margaret's House
articles.summary: After studio tenants protested outside the City Chambers, Edinburgh councillors voted to seek a delay to the eviction of around 200 artists, groups and small businesses from St Margaret's House, who have been told to leave by 24 January 2027.

articles.headline: Di pesci, androidi e utopie. Incontro con Lee Bul
articles.headline_en: Of fish, androids and utopias: a meeting with Lee Bul
articles.summary: Interview with the South Korean artist, whose installation caused controversy at MoMA, about her touring exhibitions and new collaborations.

articles.headline: Big hair with the pre-Raphaelites, 17 Orkney stand-outs and night frights in Derry: the week in art
articles.summary: Jonathan Jones's weekly roundup: William Morris and the Pre-Raphaelites at the Fitzwilliam in Cambridge, a celebration of Orkney artists at Stromness harbour, and Halloween-themed art in Derry.
articles.author: Jonathan Jones

articles.headline: GW Contemporary targets 'cultural impact' with exhibits in gallery
articles.summary: Laguna Beach gallery GW Contemporary marks its first anniversary having run a series of exhibitions alongside its commercial business, including a current solo show.

articles.headline: Hunt for £3m painting not seen for 200 years
articles.summary: Organisers of a forthcoming exhibition at Leighton House in London are appealing for help to trace a painting valued at about £3m that has not been seen in public for roughly 220 years.

articles.headline: Der erste große MeToo-Fall der Kunstgeschichte
articles.headline_en: Art history's first big MeToo case
articles.summary: On Artemisia Gentileschi: her suffering, her self-assertion and her carefully managed public image, framed as strikingly close to today's debates.

articles.headline: Witches, clowns and a killer durian! Halloween in the Blue Mountains, in pictures
articles.summary: Photographer Maja Baska documents Halloween street festivities in North Katoomba on an analogue camera, from the whimsical to the mundane.

articles.headline: Parramatta's Powerhouse is finally here. Will the $915m project live up to the hype?
articles.summary: The new Powerhouse museum in Parramatta, western Sydney, opens after a long and costly build; the piece asks whether the A$915m project can meet expectations.

articles.headline: No arts organisation 'could afford to buy' CCA from Creative Scotland warns ex-bidder
articles.summary: An artist-led company that withdrew from the sale process for Glasgow's former Centre for Contemporary Arts building says no arts group could meet the price; the CCA closed in January and went into liquidation.

articles.headline: Abu Dhabi is gaining ground in the art market, says Christie's CEO
articles.summary: Christie's chief executive Bonnie Brennan, ahead of the house's first fine art sale in Abu Dhabi on 1 November, says she wants a regular auction calendar in the city and a wider international audience for Middle Eastern artists.

articles.headline: Kazuiki Nakahara in der Galerie Kondeyne: In diesen Blättern pulsiert und atmet es
articles.headline_en: Kazuiki Nakahara at Galerie Kondeyne: these sheets pulse and breathe
articles.summary: Review of the Japanese artist's Berlin gallery show of three-dimensional works made from paper.

articles.headline: SoCal artist says Trump administration used her fan art: 'I did not and would never consent'
articles.summary: Pasadena illustrator Devin Elle Kurtz says the US Department of Education posted an apparently AI-altered version of her Avatar: The Last Airbender fan art on X without permission. She has condemned the use but does not plan legal action because the work is based on existing IP.
articles.author: Iris Kwok

articles.headline: Lee Krasner, Jackson Pollock's long-suffering wife, steps out of his shadow at the Met's spectacular exhibition
articles.summary: Review of 'Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous' at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, arguing that the show gives Krasner top billing at last and dismantles the myth of Pollock as a solitary genius, with her collages and late paintings as the highlights.
articles.author: Murray Whyte

articles.headline: Neuer Weg in der Galerie Nierendorf: Manfred Butzmann mischt sich ein
articles.headline_en: New direction at Galerie Nierendorf: Manfred Butzmann gets involved
articles.summary: A memorial show for the East German printmaker and painter Manfred Butzmann at the Berlin gallery best known for Expressionism, with a card-players painting that mixes oil with fabric, buttons, coins and a real pair of glasses singled out.
articles.author: Jens Grandt

articles.headline: Hong Kong's M+ forges new alliance with MoMA and Centre Pompidou to redefine museum loans
articles.summary: M+ in Hong Kong, MoMA in New York and the Centre Pompidou in Paris announce a partnership to share their collections and support research, treating their holdings more like a common pool for loans.

articles.headline: Oh to Believe in Another World review: William Kentridge's amazing animated ballet of black comic pain
articles.summary: Enthusiastic review of visual artist William Kentridge's hour-long animated film, screened with Shostakovich's Tenth Symphony at a festival in Baku.

articles.headline: La street artiste romaine Laika accuse la mouvance fasciste après le saccage d'une exposition
articles.headline_en: Roman street artist Laika blames the fascist movement after an exhibition is ransacked
articles.summary: Several men broke into a Rome gallery and defaced the Italian street artist's anti-Trump and pro-Palestinian works; Laika attributes the raid to far-right circles.

articles.headline: D.C. exhibit highlights Egypt's modern and contemporary art legacy
articles.summary: 'El Marsam: Modern and Contemporary Art From Egypt' at the Middle East Institute gallery in Washington: about 45 works by 29 artists, many lent from private collections in Egypt and rarely seen in the US, on view through 11 December.
articles.author: Vanessa Larson

articles.headline: Kunst: Die Galerien sind voll, die Bilder leer. Ein Abgesang auf das Abstrakte
articles.headline_en: Art: the galleries are full, the pictures empty. A swan song for the abstract
articles.summary: Essay arguing that abstract painting, once meant to unsettle the viewer, has become mass-produced decoration, and criticising an art world that has lost its capacity for wonder.

articles.headline: Hito Steyerl in Hamburg: „Da rollt ein Tsunami aus KI-Slop, Brainrot und alten Faschismen“
articles.headline_en: Hito Steyerl in Hamburg: 'A tsunami of AI slop, brain rot and old fascisms is rolling in'
articles.summary: On Steyerl's large show 'Deine Mudda macht Show' at the Deichtorhallen, which examines how images gain power through AI, drawing on pop culture and political history.
articles.author: Marcus Woeller

articles.headline: F.A.Z.-Ausstellungskalender: Welche Museen lohnen sich im November 2026
articles.headline_en: F.A.Z. exhibition calendar: which museums are worth a visit in November 2026
articles.summary: Monthly guide to November shows, including Lovis Corinth's late work in Berlin, 'Barcelona moderna' in Munich and 'Die Blauen Reiterinnen' in Wiesbaden.

articles.headline: Nomad co-founder Nicolas Bellavance-Lecompte talks taste
articles.summary: HTSI 'talks taste' interview with the curator and architect behind the Nomad collectible design fair, covering his home, souvenirs and what he collects.

articles.headline: Kim Kardashian acquista un Monet per la battuta nel film «Ragazze a Beverly Hills», il suo preferito
articles.headline_en: Kim Kardashian buys a Monet because of the line in 'Clueless', her favourite film
articles.summary: The reality star and entrepreneur has bought a painting by Monet, citing the film's joke about a picture that looks fine from afar but is a mess up close.

articles.headline: Réouverture du Mamac : à Nice, le pari controversé d'Eric Ciotti
articles.headline_en: Reopening of the Mamac: in Nice, Eric Ciotti's controversial bet
articles.summary: Nice's mayor announces a partial reopening before the end of the year of the Mamac modern and contemporary art museum, closed since January 2024 for works, raising questions about what visitors will actually get to see.

articles.headline: Plus de 250 chefs-d'œuvre de Van Gogh, Gauguin, Cézanne, Matisse… La fabuleuse collection de Gustave Fayet s'expose à la Fondation Louis Vuitton
articles.headline_en: More than 250 masterpieces by Van Gogh, Gauguin, Cézanne, Matisse: Gustave Fayet's fabulous collection goes on show at the Fondation Louis Vuitton
articles.summary: Review of the Fondation Louis Vuitton exhibition reassembling the collection of Gustave Fayet, a little-known but major French collector of the early twentieth century.

articles.headline: Gustave Fayet, cet inconnu illustre qui se passionnait pour les arts décoratifs
articles.headline_en: Gustave Fayet, the illustrious unknown with a passion for the decorative arts
articles.summary: Companion profile of Fayet as an entrepreneur who was also an accomplished painter and designer, published alongside the Fondation Louis Vuitton show.

articles.headline: Where Is All the Art About War?
articles.summary: Julia Halperin asks why so little contemporary art about war is being shown amid global conflict, finding institutions reluctant to touch the subject and artists struggling to exhibit such work.
articles.author: Julia Halperin

articles.headline: What's New at the Museum? Stargazing, Escape Rooms, Bachelorette Parties and More
articles.summary: Museums and galleries across the US are marketing after-hours programming, from stargazing and escape rooms to date nights and bachelorette parties, to draw younger audiences.
articles.author: Sarah Bahr

articles.headline: At the Metropolitan Museum of Art, Visitors Enjoy the Music
articles.summary: On the Met Live Arts programme, which stages performances by well-known musicians in unexpected spots among the collection.
articles.author: Alix Strauss

articles.headline: Short of Space, the Hispanic Society Museum Plans an Outpost in Spain
articles.summary: The space-starved Hispanic Society Museum & Library in upper Manhattan plans a new museum in Valencia devoted to Joaquín Sorolla, the city's native son, which it hopes will also benefit the New York institution.
articles.author: Leslie Wayne

articles.headline: A Guide to U.S. Museum and Gallery Openings This Fall
articles.summary: Round-up of fall openings nationwide, including Yoshitomo Nara in New York, Dalí shown beside his predecessors in Florida and Raven Halfmoon's sculptures in Oklahoma.
articles.author: Morgan Malget and Abby McCarter

articles.headline: TorinoSette, le fiere del contemporaneo battono il tempo anche con l'avant pop di C2C
articles.headline_en: TorinoSette: the contemporary art fairs keep time, with the avant-pop of C2C too
articles.summary: Weekend preview of Turin's contemporary art fairs, noting that Artissima has commissioned a site-specific project from Franco Mazzucchelli, a pioneer of inflatable art.

articles.headline: Kunst: Warum ein Berliner Museum jetzt „Spätis“ in 23-karätigem Gold kauft
articles.headline_en: Art: why a Berlin museum is now buying 'Spätis' in 23-carat gold
articles.summary: A privately funded prize of 50,000 euros that helps public museums buy art goes to Berlin's Hamburger Bahnhof for its plan to acquire a work rendering the city's late-night corner shops in gold leaf.

articles.headline: Quant'era multiculturale Matisse: la mostra al Mudec di Milano lo racconta
articles.headline_en: How multicultural Matisse was: the Mudec show in Milan tells the story
articles.summary: Preview of the Mudec exhibition in Milan exploring how Matisse drew on non-Western art traditions and how multicultural his practice was.

articles.headline: As Día de Muertos goes mainstream, ofrendas elevated to art made as remembrance
articles.summary: As Day of the Dead goes mainstream in the US, the Tribune looks at how ofrendas have become art objects of remembrance, starting from the National Museum of Mexican Art's long-running annual exhibition in Chicago.

articles.headline: 'Wall of Crazy': public art installation features 1,516 of Trump's wildest posts
articles.summary: The LA Times Friday arts newsletter leads on a Brooklyn public art installation by Phil Buehler that hangs 1,516 of Trump's social media posts on a Bushwick fence, alongside the week's LA arts news.

articles.headline: The Stars of This Philadelphia Exhibition? Squirrels.
articles.summary: Wilmer Wilson IV's show 'SKIRL!' at ICA Philadelphia uses the eastern gray squirrel as a lens on American identity and urban space after one invaded the artist's home.
articles.author: Annabel Keenan

articles.headline: El Museo de Bellas Artes de Budapest repasa la obra de Paul Gauguin en una exposición
articles.headline_en: Budapest's Museum of Fine Arts surveys Paul Gauguin's work in an exhibition
articles.summary: The Budapest museum presents Gauguin's art, legacy and influence in a show running until February 2027.

articles.headline: Leica abre una galería en Barcelona con una exposición del fotógrafo londinense Alan Schaller
articles.headline_en: Leica opens a gallery in Barcelona with a show by London photographer Alan Schaller
articles.summary: Leica Camera opens a Barcelona space devoted to the brand and photographic culture, inaugurated with Schaller's exhibition 'Life Reimagined'.
